title: customer-orion-incident-timeline-scratchpad-maya-lee
body:
Purpose / context:
This is a scratchpad for building the internal timeline + comms draft for Customer Orion (enterprise account) — they started seeing intermittent 504s and long tail latency on streaming chat/response generation between 2026-02-13 22:30 UTC and 2026-02-14 04:10 UTC. Working notes, commands tried, raw error snippets, hypotheses, and an internal short note to send to the customer (draft) are below.

High-level summary (to distill later):
- Impact: customer reported multiple user sessions hitting streaming timeouts and 504s — primarily during peak ingestion windows (bulk chat imports). Approx 17% of requests in the window experienced >= 10s extra P95 latency, and ~3% returned 504s.
- Affected endpoints: /v1/chat/completions (streaming), /v1/generate (sync) with the same model family pinned to "orion-chat-3b-quant".
- Initial suspicion: autoscaling cold-starts + KV cache misses under bursty prefix patterns, maybe exacerbated by a recent model variant rollout (quantized variant) that changed memory working set.

Timeline (raw events)
- 2026-02-13 22:27 UTC: Customer tickets ingested: INC-4821 created (severity: high). First message: "streaming times out intermittently, huge tail latency".
- 2026-02-13 22:30 UTC: Observability alert triggered: route /v1/chat/completions p95 latency > 8s for 5m, error rate spike in region us-west-2.
- 2026-02-13 22:32 UTC: Noted a spike in cold-starts on dedicated pool for customer (dedicated-pool-orion-2). Autoscaler activity shows repeated scale-ups between 22:28-22:36.
- 2026-02-13 22:34 UTC: First internal Slack: @eng-sre pinged to look at infra; @prod-hosted-api pinged about rollout.
- 2026-02-13 22:35 UTC: Deployed model variant orion-chat-3b-quant-v2 to dedicated pool (automated rollout scheduled).
- 2026-02-13 22:45 UTC: Multiple 504 traces observed for requests that were proxied to fallback model (orion-chat-3b-quant-v1).
- 2026-02-13 23:10 UTC: Manual rollback of the automated rollout initiated (rollback to v1).
- 2026-02-13 23:35 UTC: Error rate improved but tail latency remained elevated.
- 2026-02-14 01:05 UTC: Backend traces show repeated KV cache misses and higher-than-normal memory churn on GPUs used by dedicated-pool-orion-2.
- 2026-02-14 03:50 UTC: We applied a temporary route pin (force traffic to v1) and adjusted autoscaler window to be less aggressive.
- 2026-02-14 04:10 UTC: Customer reports improvement; post-window metrics show p95 latency back to normal.

Commands / checks executed (raw)
- Check recent autoscaler events: (ran as me on ops console)
  > curl -sS -H "Authorization: Bearer $OP_API_KEY" "https://ops-api.redwood.internal/autoscaler/events?pool=dedicated-pool-orion-2&since=2026-02-13T22:00:00Z" | jq '.events[] | {ts, type, scale_delta, reason}'
  -> Output sample (truncated):
  {"ts":"2026-02-13T22:28:12Z","type":"scale_up","scale_delta":8,"reason":"cpu_pressure:burst_requests"}
  {"ts":"2026-02-13T22:30:07Z","type":"scale_up","scale_delta":12,"reason":"kv_cache_miss:high"}

- Model routing table at the time:
  > redis-cli -h routing-cache.internal HGETALL "route:customer-orion:default-model"
  -> "variant","orion-chat-3b-quant-v2","last_updated","2026-02-13T22:34:31Z"

- Replayed a failing request locally (repro sample from logs):
  > curl -v -H "Authorization: Bearer ORION-USER-TOKEN" -d '{"model":"orion-chat-3b-quant","messages":[{"role":"user","content":"imported chat payload (bulk)"}]}' https://api.redwood.ai/v1/chat/completions?stream=true
  -> Response: (timeout at 12s)
  * Connection #0 to host api.redwood.ai left intact
  < HTTP/1.1 504 Gateway Timeout
  < Date: Sat, 14 Feb 2026 00:12:03 GMT
  < Content-Type: application/json
  < Content-Length: 129
  {"error":"upstream timeout","code":"gateway_timeout","details":"request blocked on backend allocation"}

- Collected GPU memory and process snapshots from 2026-02-14 01:00 UTC (ops dump):
  > nvidia-smi --query-compute-apps=pid,process_name,used_memory --format=csv
  -> "12345,python,12034 MiB"
  -> "12366,infer-server,9800 MiB"
  -> spikes showing processes hitting memory high-water marks and swap-like behavior in host kernel logs.

Relevant error snippets from logs
- proxy logs (truncated):
  [2026-02-13T22:34:58Z] WARN proxy router: attempt_allocate backend=dedicated-pool-orion-2 model=orion-chat-3b-quant-v2 reason=mem_pressure
  [2026-02-13T22:35:01Z] ERROR proxy router: allocation_failed backend=dedicated-pool-orion-2 model=orion-chat-3b-quant-v2 err="OOM allocate failed"
  [2026-02-13T22:35:03Z] ERROR proxy router: fallback to variant=orion-chat-3b-quant-v1 status=proxy_fallback

- infer-server logs (truncated):
  [2026-02-14T01:03:12Z] ERROR infer: kv_cache_miss model=orion-chat-3b-quant key_prefix="<user-bulk-import-prefix>"
  [2026-02-14T01:03:12Z] WARN infer: sequential_batch_overflow batch_id=9873 size=48 max_prefetch=24

- kernel/dmesg (host) snippets:
  [2026-02-14T01:04:22] KERNEL: cgroup memory: usage exceeded, invoked oom-killer
  [2026-02-14T01:04:23] KERNEL: Memory cgroup out-of-memory: Kill process 12345 (python) total-vm: 34G, anon-rss: 12G

Hypotheses (ordered by likelihood)
1) Regression from model variant rollout (v2) that increased working set (quantization implementation changed layer ordering + extra temp buffers) leading to memory pressure and allocation failures during bursts. Evidence: OOM logs, mem_pressure alloc failures coincide with rollout time.
2) Autoscaler misconfiguration: scale-up happened but allocation window too slow, causing short-lived allocation failures and proxy timeouts. Evidence: repeated scale_up events and proxy allocation_fail in same minute.
3) Workload pattern: bulk chat import with highly diverse prefixes caused KV cache miss storm, increasing per-request memory needs and causing batching overflow. Evidence: kv_cache_miss logs + sequential_batch_overflow warnings.
4) Downstream hardware flakiness: one GPU node entered OOM and kernel killed processes - possible hardware or driver bug. Evidence: kernel oom-killer entries and repeated process restarts.

Immediate mitigations applied (chronological)
- Rollback v2 -> v1 (2026-02-13 23:10 UTC).
- Forced route pin to v1 for customer (2026-02-14 03:50 UTC).
- Increased autoscaler warm pool size and reduced cooldown to avoid repeated cold starts (2026-02-14 03:50 UTC).
- Added temporary per-request size cap on bulk imports (rate-limit guidance to customer; they accepted temporary limit).

Next steps / action items (who/when)
- eng-serving-runtime: run perf diff between v1 and v2 quant implementations (priority P0) — reproducer: replay bulk import workload in staging with recorded traces. Owner: Samir Khan. ETA: 2026-02-17.
- eng-sre: identify node(s) that triggered kernel OOM and validate driver/kernel versions, check for known GPU driver bugs. Owner: Jordan Patel. ETA: 2026-02-16.
- customer-success: finalize customer comms explaining cause, mitigations, and follow-up plan; include recommended throttle limits for bulk import for next 48h. Owner: Maya Lee (this doc draft). ETA: 2026-02-15 18:00 UTC.
- infra/platform: add metric for "allocator failures per minute" and alert rule when allocation_failed > 5/min for a pool. Owner: platform-eng. ETA: 2026-02-21.

Draft: internal-facing customer note (short, to send after internal sync)
Subject: Orion incident update — 2026-02-14 (summary and next steps)
Hi team,
Quick summary: Orion experienced streaming timeouts and elevated p95 due to memory pressure in their dedicated pool after an automated rollout of a quantized model variant (orion-chat-3b-quant-v2). We observed allocation failures and kernel OOM events during bursty bulk imports. Immediate actions taken: rollback to stable variant v1, forced route pin, increased warm pool, and temporary client-side import rate limits.
We are investigating root cause: perf diff between v1/v2 quant changes and checking node-level OOMs/drivers. Will follow up with technical RCA and targeted mitigation (allocator-level fixes or revert of v2 changes) by 2026-02-21.
Will post a customer-facing note after we confirm root cause.
Thanks,
Maya (on behalf of CS & Eng)

Draft: customer-facing short note (to be reviewed)
Subject: Update on recent streaming timeouts (Feb 14)
Hi <Customer Orion team>,
Thanks for the report and patience — we investigated and applied mitigations that have restored normal latency for your account. Short version: a model variant rollout increased memory usage under heavy, bursty workloads (bulk imports) and caused allocation failures that led to timeouts. We rolled back the rollout, pinned traffic to the stable variant, and adjusted autoscaling to reduce cold-starts.
We recommend throttling bulk import requests to X concurrent imports (temporary limit) while we complete a perf comparison and finalize a permanent fix. We will share a full technical RCA by 2026-02-21.
Apologies for the disruption. Please reply if you need a postmortem call.
-- Maya Lee, Customer Success

Notes / open questions (to resolve)
- Need precise reproduction steps for the kv_cache_miss pattern — Samir to run replay and capture memory/time profiles.
- Confirm whether v2 quant change introduced new temp buffers or changed allocation order (affects fragmentation).
- Check whether other customers on the same pool saw similar errors (risk surface).
- Should we proactively disable automated rollouts for dedicated pools with small warm pools? (policy discussion).

Raw attachments I've saved in ops dump (links in linked_artifacts):
- ops dump: /var/ops/dumps/orion-2026-02-14.tar.gz (uploaded to ops bucket)
- logs: s3://redwood-ops/logs/orion/2026-02-14/
- perf traces: gs://redwood-perf/orion/2026-02-14/trace-*.perf

(End of scratchpad)
